options.content:
## history_growth
Flags a run whose history grows past the number set.

spec.title: history_growth analysis runs per second
spec.description: How many times per second the analyzer history_growth ran, whatever the result. It runs when a run comes in or changes, so it follows the work of your Temporal system. There is no good or bad value of its own; 0 while your system works means no runs come in. No data only when Prometheus gets no metrics from the server; it shows 0 from the start.

spec.title: history_growth analysis runs duration p95
spec.description: The time in seconds in which 95% of the runs of the analyzer history_growth ended, over the last few minutes. Normal: well under a second. Bad: a line that climbs; large histories take longer, and a slow analyzer slows the intake of runs. No data when the analyzer did not run in that time.

spec.title: history_growth findings detected
spec.description: Findings the analyzer history_growth raised in the time range shown, a count. A finding is counted once, when it is first seen. Normal: 0, or a low number that fits your system. Bad: a jump, something new went wrong; open the findings in the Flowrensic UI to see which runs. No data only when Prometheus gets no metrics from the server; it shows 0 from the start.

spec.title: history_growth analysis failures per second
spec.description: Runs of the analyzer history_growth per second that ended with an error. Normal: 0. Bad: above 0, some runs were not judged; the error lines of the server say why. No data only when Prometheus gets no metrics from the server; it shows 0 from the start.

Findings about the timeouts and retry limits of activities, judged from the activity attempts the worker interceptor sends: a timeout or a retry limit that does not fit what was seen, an activity close to its timeout, and an activity that timed out. The panel counts the findings of this kind. It shows 0 when no worker runs the Flowrensic interceptor, and has no data only when Prometheus gets no metrics from the server.

options.content:
## Activity timeouts
Judged from the activity attempts: a timeout or a retry limit that does not fit what was seen.

spec.title: Activity timeouts findings detected
spec.description: Findings of this kind raised in the time range shown, a count. A finding is counted once, when it is first seen. Normal: 0, or a low number that fits your system. Bad: a jump; open the findings in the Flowrensic UI to see which runs or workers. It stays at 0 when no worker runs the Flowrensic interceptor. No data only when Prometheus gets no metrics from the server; it shows 0 from the start.

Judged from the deploys and what the pipeline wrote about them: two versions running side by side for too long, a deploy declared but not done, an old version still used during the rollout, runs that stopped after a deploy, and a deploy with no replay test or with a failed one. The panel counts the findings of this kind. It shows 0 when no pipeline reports its deploys, and has no data only when Prometheus gets no metrics from the server.

When a rule that judges runs is new or changed, Flowrensic applies it once to the data already stored. This section shows the findings it took back as mistaken, and the stored runs it walked and skipped. Outside such a pass the panels stay at 0 or have no data.

options.content:
## Rules on stored data
Each new or changed rule applied once to the data already stored: the findings it took back as mistaken, and the stored runs it walked and skipped.

spec.title: Findings marked mistaken
spec.description: Findings that a new version of a rule took back in the time range shown, a count. Normal: 0, or some right after a rule changed. Bad: many, the old rule raised wrong findings. No data or 0 when no rule changed in the time range.

spec.title: Stored runs walked
spec.description: Stored runs per second that a new or changed rule was applied to, one line for each rule. Normal: a burst after a rule changes, then 0. Bad: a pass that never ends; see the job stored_rules on the sustainability dashboard. No data or 0 when no rule changed.

spec.title: Stored runs skipped
spec.description: Stored runs per second that a rule could not be applied to because their history is not stored, one line for each rule. Normal: 0 or low. Bad: high, many histories are gone, for example deleted by retention, so the new rule cannot judge those runs. No data or 0 when no rule changed.
